summary: Caching Object.keys() in a variable before the loop resulted in slightly slower performance (1,388,831 vs 1,404,243 ops/sec, -1.1%). Modern JavaScript engines likely already optimize repeated Object.keys() calls, and the extra variable allocation may add overhead.

Replaced spread operator with Object.assign() and manual for-in loops. Object.assign() yielded 1,380,482 ops/sec vs baseline 1,419,329 (-2.7%). Manual for-in with hasOwn was even slower at 1,232,632 (-13.2%). V8's spread operator optimization outperforms alternatives for object cloning.

Tested multiple array concatenation strategies (concat, slice+push, manual loop). All alternatives showed either worse performance or negligible improvement (<1% variance within noise). The original spread syntax is already well-optimized by modern V8 JIT.
